name: security-winrm-endpoint-authority-review
intent: WinRM/PowerShell remoting endpoint and constrained-command authority
artifacts: Listener/auth settings, endpoint/session configuration, JEA role capabilities and command/resource consumer.
trace: Trace the authenticated caller into the exact endpoint and permitted commands/parameters, including helpers that delegate broader filesystem/process access.
experiment: Use an isolated owned endpoint and inert command stubs; compare intended constrained operation and one forbidden parameter/resource.
disproof: Remoting enabled or an available cmdlet name is not unrestricted execution; validate actual role capability and parameter binding.
repair: Constrain endpoint delegation and helper parameters, preserving intended remote administration.
branch_decisions: Resolve endpoint security descriptors, session configuration and JEA role capability files under the actual connecting principal. A constrained command can invoke a helper that holds broader authority; inspect helper inputs and executable provenance. A permitted remoting connection is not a full shell, and unrestricted administrator endpoints may be intentional.
operational_method: Expand every role capability matching the connecting principal and compute the effective merged JEA capability set; permissions merge permissively, so another role can remove a parameter restriction present in one file. Include endpoint RunAs identity, visible providers/commands and wrapper implementation. Compare a constrained command under one role with the actual combined roles in an owned endpoint fixture; one .psrc alone does not establish confinement.
